_readme: User-visible changes in the replacement app, newest first.

entries.summary: The frequency is back on speech cards on the live site, and rarer senses are marked Known or Review right on the Rarer uses sheet.
detail: Frequency had vanished from every speech card on the live site (Spanish, French, Portuguese, Czech), leaving only the rank. The app checks that the frequency file belongs to the deck's release, but on the live site the deck's address is rewritten to the releases site, so the check always failed and the frequency was dropped. The check now compares the two the same way. A local copy never showed the bug because it keeps the short address.
Rarer uses: each rare sense now has × (Review) and ✓ (Known) under it, for signed-in learners. They save to the same place as before, so marks you made earlier still show.

The 'Mark rarer senses Known or Review' button on the sheet is gone, and the meanings overview no longer has a 'Show N rarer senses' section: it lists only the card's own meanings, expressions and attached forms.

entries.summary: Settings pages can go back, not just close, and the speech-mode card front shows the vocabulary rank without the '/ 10,000' deck size.
detail: Study options → Study settings now has a ‹ in its header that returns to the Study options list; before, the only way out was ✕.
Saved words and Import known words, opened from Settings, get the same ‹ back to the Settings page they came from. ✕ still closes everything.

Everyday Speech cards print 'Vocabulary rank: 12' instead of 'Vocabulary rank: 12 / 10,000'. The 10,000 was the size of the deck, not of the language. Lyrics decks keep the total because an artist's vocabulary is a real count. The About page's demo card matches.

entries.summary: Example-sentence source icons open again (tap shows a bigger 'Open on …' link), the expressions card drops its repeated labels, and Rarer uses opens as a sheet instead of a follow-on card.
detail: Source icons (Tatoeba, IMDb, SpanishDict, Wiktionary) under example sentences did nothing when tapped. The icon was a button containing another button, which HTML doesn't allow, so the browser moved the inner 'Visit' button out and there was nothing to reveal. Tapping now pops up the source's icon at full size with 'Open on Tatoeba' and an arrow; only that opens the site, and tapping anywhere else closes it. The same fix revives the icons in the Look up sheet.

The expressions card after a correct answer no longer repeats itself: the 'Expressions' heading and the PHRASE pill on every row are gone, and the subtitle reads just 'Expressions that use this word'.

Rare senses are no longer a follow-on card after a correct answer. The 'Rarer uses' tile on the back of the card opens them (with the word's expressions) in a sheet, docked beside the card on desktop and over it on phones.
Removed the 'Rare senses after a correct answer' setting (and the now-empty 'More study options' section) from Study settings.

entries.summary: Learn New no longer bounces you to a different set: the set it lands on really has cards to learn, and if one turns out to be done it goes straight on to the next.
detail: Main cause: 105 Spanish cards have no translated meaning. Setup counts cards before their meanings load, but the deck builder drops those cards. Once everything else in a set was done, the set still said 'Learn 1 new card', built nothing, and the recount moved you elsewhere, on every fresh load. Setup now loads the landing set's meanings first (the same file Start fetches anyway) and counts again.
Starting a set waits (up to 5 seconds, behind the loading screen) for a progress sync that is still running, so the set is built from your current progress rather than the copy cached on this device.
If a set still turns out to have nothing new, it no longer drops you back on the menu with a different set highlighted. It says 'Set 7 is already done. Starting Set 8…' and opens it.
Fixed a stale cache in the set counts: whether a sibling form was seen, and the level estimate, were cached per card and could outlast a Fast Track change.

entries.summary: The study options menu is simpler: plain icon-and-text rows, two toggles that stay open and show their state, and Study settings that opens only the study controls.
detail: Rows are icon and text only: no box round each one, no filled disc behind the icon.
'Front of Card: Spanish' replaces the English → Spanish row. Tapping it flips the direction and the row updates in place without closing the menu.
'Auto Speak Flashcards' replaces Mute/Enable automatic speech. The speaker icon shows whether it is on, and tapping it keeps the menu open.
Set progress and Saved words are gone from this menu. Saved words is still in Settings → Words & data.

Study settings (was Study preferences) now opens only the study section: Show first, Speak the word, Bring back learned words, More study options. Account, theme, text size and word tools stay in the full Settings from the main page. The option to open settings this way had existed but was being ignored.

entries.summary: Cards are no longer cut off on desktop with Bigger text, keyboard hints moved off the card to beside it, and the main page groups the two vocabulary modes apart from the conjugation add-on.
detail: Bigger text zooms the page by 1.15, and the zoom also stretched every window-height measurement, so the card came out taller than the window and lost its bottom row: the rank and frequency on the front, the icons on the back. Window-height sizes now divide the zoom back out, so cards and panels fit at any browser zoom.

Keyboard hints no longer sit on the card (they covered the rank and frequency line). With room beside the card the full guide shows there by default; with less room a small keyboard button opens it; on narrow windows and touch screens there are none.
The side guide had been unreachable since the study menu took over the floating buttons, and it started collapsed for everyone. It now starts open, under a new setting key.

Main page: 'Learn vocabulary · pick one' heads Everyday Speech and Songs & artists, each described by 'Best for…' bullets, with the language name filled in. Verb conjugation sits below a divider as an optional add-on, drawn lighter.

entries.summary: Verb conjugation is now the third option on the main page, and has its own links, including one for a single verb.
detail: The main page's choice of Everyday Speech or Music & lyrics now has a third option, Verb conjugation, for Spanish, Portuguese and Czech. Each language says whether it has a drill in config (conjugationDrill); French and the rest show no option until their deck exists.
New links: #/es/conjugate opens the drill for a language, #/es/conjugate/tener drills one verb. A language with no drill opens that language instead.
The drill page now keeps its address up to date: the verb you're drilling, or the verb and tense whose table you're reading. Copy the address bar and it reopens exactly that.

entries.summary: Spotify sign-in now sends one fixed callback address for the live site, so it works again after the move to Fluency-App and no longer depends on which address the app was opened from.
detail: Spotify only accepts callback addresses registered in its dashboard. The app used to build one from whatever page it was on, so the rename from Fluency-Next to Fluency-App (and the app/ mirror) each needed their own entry. rabbijoshy.github.io now always uses https://rabbijoshy.github.io/Fluency-App/callback.html, set in config under publicServices.spotifyRedirectUris. Local dev servers still build their own.
The callback page's fallbacks went to the bare site root, which is a 404 on GitHub Pages. They now go back to the app.
Sign-in tokens are only passed between pages on the same site, and the app ignores token messages from anywhere else.
The web app manifest now names its scope and id explicitly.

entries.summary: The deck wheel now appears earlier and waits for you — tap to continue, or it moves on after five seconds.
detail: The wheel used to hold for under a second, and the numbers only finished animating at about three quarters of that — so there was barely a moment to read them. It now stays until you tap it, and gives up after five seconds if you don't.

It also appears earlier in the load. The figure only needs the word list, not the level buttons, so the rest of the screen is now built behind the wheel instead of before it — less of the wait is time added for its own sake.
'Tap to continue' appears once the wheel has finished filling, never before.
Reduced-motion still gets the pause to read, just without the animation.
The setup path now prints its own timings to the console, so how long each step takes can be measured rather than guessed.

entries.summary: The progress wheel now belongs to opening a language or mode, not a 20-card set, and Review home leads with how reviews are timed.
detail: Opening a language or a lyrics deck spins as before, then — once the deck's data has arrived — shows a big wheel of your progress across that whole deck, with the comprehension figure under it.
Small set loads are back to a plain spinner. The wheel is still wired up there and can be switched back on.
Review home now opens with whether spaced repetition is on, above the counts it governs, with a ? beside it.

That ? opens a short plain-English explanation of how review timing works: get a word right and it waits longer, get it wrong and it comes back soon. No intervals, no algorithm. It stacks over Review home rather than replacing it, and links on to the setting.

entries.summary: Fast Track has its switch back on the main page, the sheet leads with what it means, and skipped words now name the word they actually matched.
detail: The Fast Track row on the main page has a switch again — one tap turns it on without opening anything. Tapping the rest of the row opens the Fast Track page, and until you have opened it once the row invites you to.
That page now starts with the explanation, and both controls are open on it instead of hidden behind a Fine-tune button. The 'Saved on this device' line and the second on/off switch are gone.
The skipped and merged word lists live inside the step that creates them, as they did before. The skipped-word decks moved below the controls.

Skipped and merged word rows are shorter: a gloss's bracketed qualifier and its extra senses are trimmed, so 'to abandon (leave behind)' reads 'to abandon'. Searching still finds the words that were trimmed away.

A skipped word can now show the word it actually matched, with an arrow. Until now it showed the card's first meaning, which was picked for the card and had nothing to do with why the word was skipped. Decks need rebuilding before the arrows appear.

entries.summary: The conjugate drawer now only shows the matching tense. Study options and Meanings and expressions dock at the side, and keyboard hints sit in the gutter instead of on the card.
detail: Conjugate on the card back lists the tense that contains this form, with a link into conjugation mode for the rest.
Study options opens as a side sheet and takes a gutter before anything else. Meanings and expressions replace a weaker sheet when only one gutter is free.
Keyboard shortcuts sit in the left gutter on a wide screen and hide when they would cover the card.

entries.summary: Portuguese and Czech can now open conjugation mode. On a large screen the drill is bigger, and Back to study leaves the page.
detail: The conjugate drawer now links Portuguese and Czech into conjugation mode, using the existing verbecc and Kaikki tables.
Czech still only has present and imperative — that is the source table, not a missing drill.
A Back to study control returns to the card. Desktop drill cards and tables are larger.

entries.summary: Opening a deck now animates your progress on that set, and the home screen folds Fast Track and Review into one button each.
detail: Tapping a set you have already started replaces the spinner with a large ring that animates your known / review / unseen split for that set. It paints from figures the home screen already holds, so it appears before any deck data is fetched.
The ring holds for about nine tenths of a second, then the cards appear — tap the screen to skip the wait. A set you have never studied keeps the plain spinner, with no added delay.
Fast Track is one row on the home screen. The on/off switch, the skipped-word decks and the skipped / merged word lists all moved into the Fast Track sheet behind it.

The review section is now Review & Progress, with two buttons: Review home, a sheet listing what is waiting by urgency, by level and against your overall progress; and Quick review, which starts 20 cards straight away.
Quick review takes the 20 most needed cards — never-got-right first, then recent mistakes, then overdue.

entries.summary: Language colours stay saturated. Dark mode lightens them and light mode darkens them, without washing them toward white or black.
detail: Portuguese, Spanish, Czech and the other languages keep their flag hue. The button colour is a lighter saturated shade in dark mode and a darker saturated shade in light mode.
Label colour is chosen so the text still clears the button.

entries.summary: Fix: the frequency had disappeared from the bottom of the card in Merge Lemmas mode.
detail: A card shows a figure again in merged mode. The previous change showed only the printed form's own figure, and blanked the card when the source does not list that form.
The card now says whose figure it is: its own, 'All forms' for a family total, or the named form the source did measure.
Long-press still pins the per-form breakdown.

entries.summary: First login explains why words are ordered by frequency, and the main page follows each language's colours.
detail: A three-sentence intro appears the first time you sign in, with a clear Skip intro button.
Setup buttons use a light tint of the language colour in dark mode and a dark shade in light mode, with the flag's second colour as a thin edge.
Settings has a Normal / Bigger text size. Example sources open a Visit Tatoeba or Visit IMDb box. Side panels sit in the middle of the gap beside the card.

entries.summary: The frequency on a card now shows which forms it counts, and says it counts the spelling rather than the sense.
detail: Long-press the frequency on the front of a card to pin a breakdown listing each source-listed form and its own published figure, commonest first.
A tap still gives the short note; the pinned list stays until you tap again, since a total across eight forms cannot be read inside a tap.
Wording corrected: the published list is keyed on spelling and blind to part of speech, which is also why an interjection carries a figure at all.
Every number shown is one the source publishes. Nothing is split or apportioned across merged forms (decision 0024).

entries.summary: Non-decompositional phrases now leave the parent card and show as their own follow-up after a correct answer.
detail: PHRASE senses from the MWE inventory are no longer extra senses on the word card.
Marking the word correct always opens a separate expressions child card, independent of rare senses.
That follow-up cannot be turned off in Settings, because those expressions are meant to be learned.

entries.summary: Find a word now lives in Settings, and on a computer ⌘F or Ctrl+F opens a Spotlight-style search bar.
detail: Removed Find a word from the study options sheet; Settings → Your words is the button.
⌘F / Ctrl+F intercepts the browser find shortcut and opens a centred search overlay.
Arrow keys move through matches; Escape and the backdrop dismiss it.

entries.summary: Spanish set-1 function words now group lookalike English senses (it/him/you, a/an, of/from) on the same card, without rerunning WSD.
detail: A keep-list overlay merges sibling senses on que, de, a, lo, un, una, al, le, del, and se after the deck loads.
Existing example assignments stay on the merged leaf; the heading is a slash-join of the original English glosses.
Those cards show a short grammar line; del and al also link to de+el and a+el.

entries.summary: The desktop card is 5% narrower, the stacked-deck cards behind it are gone, and side panels now shrink to fit a narrower window, so they dock from about 1180px wide instead of 1360px.
detail: Desktop card width 540px to 513px. Phones are unaffected: every use of the width sits under the 768px desktop breakpoint.
Removed the ghost cards that peeked out either side of the card to suggest a deck, with their light-theme rules and the class toggles that drove them.

Side panels take the space beside the card, 16px from the screen edge and 16px clear of the card, up to 400px and shrinking to 300px. Below 300px nothing docks. In a set that means docking from about 1180px wide; it was 1360px.
The panel width is measured from the real card, so changing the card's size no longer needs the docking rules touched.
On the setup page sheets now dock from 900px wide; it was 1024px.
Repaired the service worker's pre-cache list, which an earlier commit had rolled back: side-dock.js was missing and two entries pointed at old files.

entries.summary: Cleaner inline Details, sensible card expansion and summaries of visible meanings.
detail: Details / Hide replaces More details and its counter. The gloss, control and supporting information share a line where space permits.
Opening details recalculates available height; empty space above the bottom buttons can move the example down before meanings need to scroll.
Meaning summaries and +N use emitted rows rather than the complete inventory, so hidden meanings do not appear in the preview.

Expanded Portuguese and Spanish review: shared rules remove repeated clauses, shorten usage boilerplate and place semantic explanations before bracketed constructions. Long contexts use full-width rows on phones.
Verified 127 app tests, 134 expanded group/width checks across 40 release-card fixtures, and 12 normal/enlarged text checks.

entries.summary: Readable meaning distinctions across Portuguese, Czech and Spanish, with the release-card audit completed.
detail: Essential context remains visible before selecting a subsense; long explanations wrap and phone groups stack when needed. Meaning text is at least 13px and supporting badges at least 12px.
Portuguese keeps a bit of and article-use explanations; Spanish preserves place/time/manner; Czech keeps reflexive distinctions and separates case requirements from companion words.

Checked all six metadata families across 30,000 cards, compared shared-gloss cues in the first 1,000 per language, and reviewed 20 real-card fixtures across 82 expanded group/width combinations. Source defects are recorded in docs/ui/SENSE_METADATA_AUDIT.md.

entries.summary: The app's word and song files now load from a separate release site, so app updates go live in about a minute instead of several.
detail: Release files (about 1 GB) moved to their own GitHub Pages site, rabbijoshy.github.io/Fluency-Releases/. The app site now republishes only the app on each deploy.

Config still names releases as releases/…; the new js/release-host.js maps that to the release site. A local dev server serving the app at its root keeps reading its own /releases/, so unpublished releases stay testable.
The old unused v12 display-v4 decks (842 MB) were removed from the app site.
The app repo is being renamed from Fluency-Next to Fluency-App; old links are forwarded.

entries.summary: Fixed the app not starting: the last deploy shipped a card file that needed a newer sense-metadata module than the one on the site.
detail: The previous deploy's flashcards.js imports readableSenseNote and senseMetadataPeers from card-metadata-pills.js, but the site still served the older card-metadata-pills.js, so the app stopped on load for everyone.
Shipped the matching card-metadata-pills.js under a new version tag, with new tags for flashcards.js and main.js and a new service-worker cache, so browsers fetch the matched pair.

entries.summary: Rare senses and expressions are separate study settings, Fast Track sits in the level picker, and source links ask once before leaving the app.
detail: Settings → More study options now has two toggles: rare senses after a correct answer, and expressions after a correct answer. Turning one off no longer hides the other.
Fast Track is no longer a Settings row. It lives under Choose level, in the same box as the level buttons, because it changes which cards that level contains.
Dictionary, subtitle and Look up destinations no longer open a new tab on the first tap. The first tap shows a leave-site icon; that icon is what actually opens the other website.

entries.summary: Settings now opens on the left on a wide screen, and anything you open from it stacks on top of it; a second card panel opens on the left when the left is free, so two can be read side by side.
detail: Left is you and the app: settings, with whatever is opened from it (saved words, Fast Track, progress, find word) stacked on top, so closing the top one returns you to settings. Otherwise progress, saved words, shortcuts and help.

Right is this card: dictionary, synonyms, conjugation, card data, lyric breakdown, rarer-sense knowledge and word search. When the right is taken and the left is free, the next one opens on the left; when both are taken it replaces the one on the right.
Settings takes the left: opening it closes a card panel that had spilled there.
Card panels on either side close when the card changes or flips to its front; settings and its stack stay open while you study, and stay open if you leave the set.
Escape closes the right-hand panel first, then whatever is stacked over settings, then settings, and never leaves the set while one is open.
On the setup page (1024px and wider) settings also opens on the left, with the word lists on the right.
Fast Track, built as a full page, becomes a sheet when stacked over settings: its close button now sits on the sheet rather than in the screen corner.
Narrower windows and phones are unchanged.

entries.summary: About: the two animated cards are now the way into the walkthrough, the Speech card is banco (bank / bench), and "What's under the hood" is short, plain bullets.
detail: Tapping either animated card opens the walkthrough on that card; the Lyrics card opens straight on the Lyrics screen. A caption under the pair says so, and the separate button is gone.
The cards sit directly after the opening two paragraphs, side by side on desktop with their text underneath; on a phone each card is followed by its own text.

The Speech example is banco (bank / bench) instead of que. Two meanings nobody could confuse, and every example in the live deck is right, so a quick look shows what matching meanings to sentences is for. The walkthrough uses it too.
"What's under the hood" is eight short bullets about what each step does for a learner, not how it is implemented.

entries.summary: About refreshed: the pipeline is described step by step, and the two animated cards now look like today's cards and show the same que and cielo as the walkthrough.
detail: "What's under the hood" walks through the six pipeline steps: choosing words by how often they are said, collecting translated subtitle lines, dictionary sense menus, the append-only ledger of judgements, picking the meaning in each sentence (embeddings plus grammar, companion-word and alignment checks, abstaining when unsure), and building the deck.
Corrected: About said meanings were chosen by asking Gemini. They are chosen from Gemini embeddings plus local checks; no model writes the answer.
The animated About cards use the walkthrough's own real cards (que, cielo) instead of hand-written ones. fuego is gone; its "light" example did not show that meaning.
They now draw meanings the way a live card does: part-of-speech colour, a tick on the chosen meaning, the four-bar meter instead of "≈50%", and the studied word underlined in the example.
Prose no longer quotes percentages the cards no longer show.

entries.summary: Everything that doesn't move you within your set now opens at the side on a wide desktop: dictionary, synonyms, conjugation and card data dock beside the card, and session sheets stay open while you study.
detail: Right side, about this card: dictionary, synonyms, conjugation, card data, lyric breakdown, rarer-sense knowledge and word search. One at a time; opening one closes the other.
Right-side panels close when the card changes or flips to its front, because what they show gives the answer away.
Left side, about the session: saved words, progress, shortcuts and help. One at a time, and they stay open while you flip, grade and move between cards; the card is no longer blocked behind them.
Conjugation docks beside the card instead of taking over the screen; narrower windows and phones keep the full-screen table.
Escape now closes the nearest open panel instead of leaving the set.
Leaving the study view closes anything docked in it.
Rarer uses is unchanged: it moves you onto a temporary card, so it is not a side panel.
New module js/side-dock.js holds the rule, so the individual panels only call into it.

entries.summary: Tutorial, walkthrough and About are now three separate things: About links a short two-screen walkthrough for visitors, the "?" tutorial stays for learners, and About is visible again to logged-out visitors.
detail: New walkthrough (js/walkthrough.js), opened only from About's "See a card, annotated" button and closing back into About. Screen 1 shows the front and back of a card side by side with every part labelled at once; screen 2 is a Lyrics card. On a phone the card turns over in place, so it is three screens.

Labels are callouts with leader lines where there is room beside the card, and short tags pinned onto it where there is not. The card stays live: tap a meaning and the example changes; Spotify plays the real line.
About no longer closes itself and opens the learner tutorial. "Start tutorial" in About is gone.
The learner tutorial is unchanged in behaviour and renamed for what it is: js/tutorial.js, #cardTutorialModal, .card-tutorial-*. The in-study prompt now says "tutorial", not "walkthrough".
The card both show is js/card-replica.js, shared rather than copied.
Fix: About was invisible to logged-out visitors. It opened underneath the landing card (z-index 1000 vs 30001), so ?about=1 showed only the login card. It now stacks above it.
Fix: reopening the tutorial no longer shows the previous run's "The back of the card" heading over the setup intro.

entries.summary: On a wide desktop, reference sheets now open at the side instead of over the middle: synonyms docks beside the card, session sheets dock left, and the setup page's word lists open as a right-hand sheet.
detail: One rule decides placement: a sheet you read while still looking at what is behind it docks to a side; a task that takes your attention (sign-in, settings, imports, language picker, Fast Track, end of deck) stays centred.

Study session, 1360px and wider: the right gutter is about this card (find word, lyric breakdown, rare senses, and now synonyms); the left gutter is about the session (saved words, study progress, keyboard shortcuts, help). The card stays fully visible.

Synonyms is hosted on the page while open, as the conjugation panel already was, because the card's flip transform clips anything inside it. It closes when the card flips to the front, since its headword would give the answer away in English-to-target mode, and a card change removes it.

Setup page, 1024px and wider: merged forms, skipped words, extras, saved words, cognate rules, progress, help and shortcuts open as a right-hand sheet over the progress sidebar, with the steps still readable behind a light dim.
Narrower windows and phones are unchanged.
Synonyms data currently exists only in the lyrics decks; the v15 speech decks carry none.

entries.summary: Example sentences are now ordered by four plain rules instead of a scoring cascade: a translated, single-sentence, confidently-disambiguated line leads, and the dictionary's own example sits second.
detail: First line picked by four keys in order: has an English translation, is a single sentence, WSD confidence tier (cheap-agree > leaf > glosskey > tuple), reinforces a word missed in the last week. Ties keep deck order.
Confidence ranks rather than gates. Gating on it would have pushed 79.8% of cards onto a dictionary first line; ranking leaves only 1.1% of senses without a usable corpus sentence.

The canonical dictionary example moved from last to second. It never leads while a real corpus line exists: 9.3% of canonical lines run to two sentences and only 44.6% contain the card's own surface form, so it often has nothing to underline.

Dropped the easiness score (an opaque composite, and `easiness || 999999` was inverting the 15.9% of examples that score exactly 0, sorting the easiest lines last), the 6-14 token length window (the pipeline already caps length) and deck-word overlap (sentence length in disguise at 3.5k cards).
Multi-sentence detection ignores abbreviations, which were 10.9% of everything the pattern caught.
rankConfidentWsdExamples no longer sorts twice and throws the first result away.
Measured over all 28,661 senses in the live v15 deck: the first line changes for 3.9% of them.

entries.summary: 'Take me to my level' no longer sends you to set 1 and then quietly correct itself
detail: Every set count on the setup screen is read from your progress, and an empty progress map read identically whether you had studied nothing or the fetch simply had not landed yet. Rendering on the second marked every set unseen and dropped you at set 1 of level 1 — then the next render, once progress arrived, filled the boxes in correctly. That is the glitch-and-refresh.

Progress now says explicitly when it has been looked up, and the level and set renderers wait for that answer before choosing where to send you. A four-second cap means an unreachable connection still draws the screen rather than leaving it empty, and it gives up once rather than once per render.
This covers the Fast Track case too: remembered Fast Track settings are reconciled in the same reply, so they are settled before the counts are computed.

entries.summary: The skipped-words and merged-forms lists show the English word again on Spanish, Portuguese and Czech
detail: The setup screen loads the skinny index — id, word, rank, lemma and nothing else — so there was no translation to print and every row's English column came out blank. French looked fine only because it is still on the older single-file index that ships meanings inline; Spanish, Portuguese and Czech are all on the sharded v15 format and were all equally blank. It reads as a Portuguese problem because Portuguese is where you happened to look.

The English word is now fetched as rows scroll into view, a study set at a time. The excluded list runs to thousands of words, so pulling every shard up front would download most of the deck just to label a list.
A row hydrated this way also becomes findable by its English word in the filter box.

entries.summary: The word above the card and the word underlined in the example are now the same answer, and accents no longer break the match
detail: The header and the underline each decided independently which form an example was about, and could disagree: when a pooled example had no recorded sibling form, the header fell back to the card's representative surface and showed 'buena' over a line reading 'buenos' — while the underline, which does check the sentence, matched nothing and highlighted nothing. Both halves of that were one cause. They now read a single resolver.

Occurrence matching was the one comparison in the card that was accent-sensitive, so a card on 'estás' found nothing in a line spelling it 'estas'. Subtitles and lyrics drop accents constantly. Matching now folds accents the way the rest of the card already did.
Enclitic pronouns are peeled: a card on 'verte' now finds 'ver' in the line, and 'dármelo' finds 'dar'. Up to two pronouns come off, longest first.

When nothing recorded appears in the sentence, the closest form of the word in that sentence is found by shared stem — conservatively, since a wrong underline is worse than none: never for words under four letters, and never across a long tail. Anything reached this way is marked with a dashed underline and says it is the closest form, not a recorded one.
The form shown is always the spelling the sentence actually carries, so the header cannot print a stem that is not a word.

entries.summary: The example footer stops fighting itself: source credit and tick strip each get half the row, and the provenance icon leads its title
detail: The IMDb/Wiktionary/Tatoeba icon now sits to the left of its title. It was to the right, which meant a long film title pushed the icon off the row entirely.

Source credit and the tick strip each own exactly half the row and can no longer take the other's space. Previously the credit was free-growing against an unbounded wrapping strip, so a long title and a thirty-example strip fought over one row.

The tick strip squeezes through two density tiers measured against the width it actually got, and only clips once the tightest tier still overflows — and when it clips, it keeps the current tick in view, so the position cue survives.

Ticks no longer shrink to fit: without an explicit no-shrink they compressed into slivers, which looked like fitting while making the current position indistinguishable. The density tiers give way in visible steps instead.

entries.summary: Top bar reads as one line again, conjugation settings lead with what matters, and the language's colour is back as a trim
detail: The language chip stacked the flag above the language name, which read as two unrelated controls. Flag and name now sit side by side on one row at every width.
Every icon in the main-page top bar is larger (50px target, 27px glyph; 46/25 on phones) — they were sitting at the 44px accessibility floor rather than a size chosen for legibility.
The 'Update ready' pill was clipped to 'Update rea' on every phone by a hardcoded 92px cap. It now gets its content and the language chip is the one that shortens.

Conjugation mode setup now opens on Verb type, How common, Tenses, Persons and Easy mode; Patterns, Repetition, Prompt and the data-provenance note are folded into Advanced settings, which summarises itself while closed.

The per-language colour is visible again as a trim on the language chip and a hairline under the top bar. The setup panel keeps its neutral accent, so switching to Spanish no longer threatens to turn every control flag-red. Dark flag colours (Czech, Portuguese, Italian) are lifted to a lightness floor so every language actually shows one.

entries.summary: Settings are simpler, with Fast Track saved per language and word import and export easy to find
detail: The main Settings view now shows study choices, direct import and export actions, an account link and a single theme row instead of a long tab list.
Fast Track has one switch per language and optional fine-tuning for word forms and familiar words; turning it back on restores the learner’s choices.
Signed-in Fast Track choices sync through progress metadata across devices. Skipped-word decks remain in the main study menu.
Import and export are also available from Words & data and all-time Progress.

entries.summary: Front-card part-of-speech and lemma pills now fit their words instead of stretching across empty space
detail: Pill groups keep the existing count-based layout and maximum widths, but each visible capsule fits its label and stays centred.
Long lemmas can still use the available width and shrink their label size when needed.

entries.summary: Rarer-uses list now scrolls by swipe, the surface form stops jumping between senses, and sense metadata is readable again
detail: The rarer-senses list inherited touch-action: none from the card (set there so a drag grades the card), which disabled the browser's own scrolling and left the scrollbar as the only way to move the list. Vertical drags are handed back to the browser and the scrollbar is hidden.

The lemma line under the word appeared for one sense and vanished for the next, shunting the surface form up and down the card. The slot is now held open for any card whose senses disagree about the citation form, so only the lemma changes.
Sense metadata pills had a 9px floor in a muted colour — 'indicating time' on en was effectively illegible. Minimum type is now 10px (11px undense) and the grammar tier carries real contrast.

entries.summary: 10,000-card V15 speech releases deployed for Spanish, Portuguese, and Czech
detail: Composed, validated, and activated full 10,000-card Speech decks (es-speech-v15-10000x10, pt-speech-v15-10000x10, cs-speech-v15-10000x10) from KILN 2's published Stage 04 assignments.
Every deck is sharded into 500 study sets with 100% valid meanings across all sets, preserving SENTENCE_FLOW ticks with canonical examples and multi-word expression routing.

entries.summary: The tutorial card gets its colour back, stops cutting off senses, and sizes itself to what it is showing
detail: The card was grey because the replica used the live card's colour rules but never set the variable that feeds them. Part-of-speech colour is back: the sense group is tinted and edged in its colour, the selected sense is outlined and ticked in it, the prominence bars carry it, and the word you are studying is picked out and underlined in it inside the example, the way it is on a real card.

Sense rows were being cut off. The Portuguese card lost a whole sense and the grammar pills under the selected one. The card now measures what it is showing and takes the height it needs, instead of a fixed height that was too short for the dense cards and too tall for the sparse ones.
On a phone the densest cards want more height than the screen has, so the guided tour scrolls whatever it is explaining into view rather than leaving it hidden.

The rank and the frequency now sit at opposite ends of the foot of the card, as they do when you are studying, and read Vocabulary rank: 1 / 6,000 and Frequency: 33,170/million, the real figures from the Spanish deck.
More space between the header, the senses and the example, and a little more inset from the card edge, so borders are not running into each other.

entries.summary: Conjugation mode: the clue settings are now a single Easy mode switch instead of three options
detail: Easy mode is one checkbox. It tints the infinitive on the question side with what this card does — tener is orange on tengo and tú tienes, green on nosotros and vosotros — and prints a line above naming the family the verb belongs to, like venir, pensar.

The two cues do not overlap, so there is no reason to choose between them: the colour says whether the stem changes here, the line says what kind of verb it is and leaves you to know which persons the pattern reaches.
This replaces the separate No clue / Name the pattern / Easy radio. Default is off.

entries.summary: Conjugation mode: a Clues setting — colour the prompt by what this card does, or name the family the verb belongs to
detail: Easy mode tints the infinitive on the question side with this card's own form type, before you answer. Green means the stem does not change here, orange means it does. Because it is per card and not per verb, tener comes up orange for tengo and green for tenemos, which is the association worth building.

Name the pattern is the middle setting: it says which family the verb belongs to — like volver, poder — without saying whether the pattern applies to this particular person. You still have to know that nosotros sits outside the stress pattern.

The family is taken from the present indicative, not from counting every tense. Counting everything made tener an en to uv verb, because the tuv- stem spans the preterite and two subjunctives; true, but not how anyone thinks of it.
The example verbs are chosen by how common they are, not alphabetically, so the o-ue family is introduced as like volver, poder rather than like acordar, acostar.
Default is no clue. The setting lives under Clues on the Choose screen.
The conjugation page's own script and stylesheet now carry ?v= tags, so a deploy is picked up instead of being served from cache.

entries.summary: Conjugation mode: the pronoun sits above the verb, answers are read out loud, endings are coloured, and the fonts now match the cards
detail: The pronoun moved above the infinitive. You read who it is, then which verb, then produce the form, instead of looking above and below the verb to work out what is being asked.

The answer is read out loud when it is revealed, using the study app's own voice module rather than a second copy of it, so a conjugation is spoken by the same voice, chosen by the same quality scoring, as a flashcard. Press s to hear it again. There is a Read the answer out loud switch under Prompt if you want to drill in silence.

The ending is coloured and the stem is dimmed, on the cards and in the tables. tengo and tienes carry the stem-change colour on -o and -es while tenemos and tenéis carry the regular colour on -emos and -éis, so what changes and what does not is visible at a glance.

The colouring is only applied where the split is honest. Compound tenses, off-model forms like voy, and anything whose ending the model could not identify are left whole rather than split at a guessed boundary.
The page now uses the app's three fonts — DM Sans for prose, Space Grotesk for the words being learned, JetBrains Mono for figures — instead of the system stack.

entries.summary: Conjugation mode: tenses are now in English, in the order a learner meets them, with the rare ones folded away
detail: The tense list was in the source's own alphabetical order, which opened on Imperativo Afirmativo and buried the present indicative in the middle. It now runs Indicative, then Subjunctive, then Imperative, and within each mood: present, preterite, imperfect, future, conditional, then the perfect tenses, then the archaic ones.

Tense and mood names are shown in English — Present, Preterite, Imperfect, Present perfect — rather than Presente, Pretérito, Pretérito perfecto. This applies on the cards and in the Tables dropdown too.
The two imperative moods are folded into one Imperative heading with Affirmative and Negative under it, because that is one mood to a learner.

Each mood shows only what a first course covers and hides the rest behind a + 4 rarer tenses link: Indicative opens with six of its ten, Subjunctive with two of its six. Picking all in a mood reveals them.
A tense the name table does not cover keeps its source name, sorts last and counts as rare, rather than being silently ranked.

entries.summary: Show original Speech-list frequencies and place reference views beside desktop cards
detail: Restored released-word frequency values from the pinned EsPal, Lexique, Portuguese FrequencyWords, and Czech FrequencyWords source lists, with source and unit recorded for every language.
Merged-lemma cards now sum those source-listed form frequencies for their front-of-card figure; harvested example sentences no longer supply a misleading per-million number.
Spanish and French use per-million rates. Portuguese and Czech show source-list occurrence counts because those published lists do not provide a per-million denominator.
On wide desktop screens, Find a word, lyric breakdown, and card knowledge open to the right of the visible card; smaller screens keep the existing sheet layout.

entries.summary: Conjugation mode: the off-model pattern no longer calls itself one-offs while listing the verbs that share it
detail: Forms whose ending does not match the model at all were labelled no shared pattern, one-offs, and then immediately listed three other verbs that behave the same way. They are off the model, not one-offs, and the chip now says so.

entries.summary: Conjugation mode: a separate drill page for verb patterns, reached from the conjugate drawer on the back of a card
detail: The conjugate drawer now has a Drill this verb in conjugation mode button above the external paradigm link. That link is the only way in, so the new page and the study app can be worked on without treading on each other. It appears only for languages that have a deck built; Spanish has one today.
Conjugation mode is its own page at /conjugation/, sharing no HTML, CSS or JS with the study app. Choose what you want to drill, drill it, or look up a full paradigm.

Choose has eight collapsed sections, each showing its own current selection on the right, so the whole menu of options is readable on a phone without opening anything: tenses, verb type, patterns, repetition, how common, persons, prompt direction, provenance.

Verb type (regular, spelling change, stem change, irregular) is recomputed against the tenses you picked, so tener counts as irregular when the present is selected and regular when only the imperfect is.
Patterns lists every stem alternation found in the data with example verbs, so you can drill just the o-ue group or just the one-offs.

Repetition offers one card per lesson: the present indicative of the 193 commonest verbs is 1,154 forms but only 53 distinct lessons, and coverage mode shows each lesson once, taught by a verb picked at random from the verbs that share it.

The drill has no buttons. Space or tap reveals, space again advances, left arrow goes back, swipe moves, and t opens the full table on the tense you just missed. The answer names the pattern and the verbs that share it.
Prompt direction can be flipped to show the English meaning instead of the infinitive.
Tables takes a verb by search and one tense from a dropdown, rather than listing every tense at once.
Nothing is scored, stored or scheduled yet. This is the selection layer only.

How the patterns are worked out: for each form the builder takes the commonest ending for verbs of that class in that tense and person, strips it, and records the minimal edit from the infinitive's stem to the stem actually used. pens to piens is e-ie; busc to busqu is c-qu. Two forms are the same lesson when class, tense, person, ending and that edit all match. No verb is hand-tagged, and the same code runs for Portuguese, French and Czech.
Service worker cache bumped to flashcards-v496; style.css and light-theme.css version tags bumped.

entries.summary: Give card grammar labels a steady layout and make setup controls clearer
detail: Reserved consistent capsule layouts for one, two, three, and larger POS and lemma groups, with shared font fitting for long labels.
Added breathing room around desktop card content while keeping the phone layout compact.
Grouped account, tutorial, and settings controls on the right of the setup bar and made language a clearer two-line button on the left.
Centred the Choose level and Your next set headings and made each heading and its information icon one help button.

entries.summary: Show sense commonness once and let learners mark rarer senses deliberately
detail: Removed the repeated commonness bar from a collapsed sense heading when it contains only one visible subrow.
Added an opt-in rarer-senses section to the knowledge menu and an entry point on the Rarer uses page.
Saved explicit rare-sense Known or Review choices as stable item progress; rare Review can return in focused review without marking the whole word known.

entries.summary: The tutorial now opens by walking through the real setup screen, and Lyrics mode gets a slide of its own instead of appearing unannounced
detail: The intro is no longer three tick-boxes filling themselves in. It is a replica of the setup screen you actually use, and a pointer moves through it: pick a language, pick whether you want everyday speech or song lyrics, pick a level, pick a set. Each choice holds long enough to read before the next one.
It ends on a live Learn 20 new cards button and waits. You open the first card yourself.

The order is now front of the card, back of the card, then a slide explaining what Lyrics mode is, then a Lyrics card. Previously the deck changed silently and the Lyrics card had to explain itself in its own annotations.

The Lyrics slide says the three things that are actually different: the example is a real lyric, you can play it in Spotify, and the number counts that artist's lines rather than the language at large.
Removed the Speech and Lyrics labels from the header and the step counter. They named two modes before you had met either one.
Underneath, the walkthrough is now a plain list of steps rather than two decks with two faces each, so the order of the story is one list to read and to change.

entries.summary: The Fast Track details page now uses the width of the window, states each count once, and no longer reports a verified zero it never counted
detail: The page was capped at 1040px and stacked each explanation above its own controls, so it read as a thin ribbon down the middle of a wide window while the prose wrapped into a narrow column. It now runs to 1480px, and inside each card the explanation sits beside the example and the controls rather than above them, which spends the spare width and cuts the height roughly in half. Below 1180px the card stacks again; below 420px the two cards stack.

Each count appeared twice -- once on the button as '(2707)' and again underneath as '2,707 flashcards merged' -- in two wordings written by two different functions. The info lines are gone. The button carries the figure and says what it is: 'View 2,707 merged forms'.

'View skipped words (0)' is fixed. A zero could mean the vocabulary had not loaded yet, and the button announced it as a counted result. Nothing is now claimed until the words have actually been counted; when they have been and none matched, the page says so in a sentence instead of showing an empty button.
Spanish does have a cognate map -- 4,915 of its 6,000 Speech words carry a score and 1,128 clear the shipped cutoff. The zero came from the map not being in memory yet at the moment the page counted.

Fixed the underlying race: an in-flight cognate-map fetch was not keyed by language, so switching language could make the second language join the first one's load and then record itself as loaded with no scores attached.

entries.summary: Tutorial fixes: a slower setup intro you dismiss yourself, plainer wording, the lemma back on the front, and no more numbered badges
detail: The setup preview now holds on each step long enough to read, and stops on the last one with a live Start set button. You open the first card yourself instead of it racing past. Skip intro still leaves at any point.
The front of a card says Frequency: 21,340/million instead of 'Frequency from the Spanish release', which told you nothing. Same wording and same figures as a real card.
The part-of-speech pill carries its lemma again, so a Portuguese card shows 'verb ter' above the form tem, the way the live card does.
Front of the card and back of the card, not question side and answer side.
Removed the numbered circles on the card and in the notes. They indexed a numbered list that the guided tour had already replaced. The element being explained is outlined in amber instead.

entries.summary: The card tutorial now opens on the question side, plays a short setup intro, and stops repeating itself on Lyrics
detail: A three-step setup preview (language, level, study set) plays for about three seconds before the first card, so the walkthrough starts where you would really start. Tap it or press Skip intro to go straight to the card.
Every chapter now shows the question side first and flips to the answer side, matching the order you meet cards when studying.
The card no longer flips when you tap it or press space. Only Continue and the mobile Next/Back buttons turn it, so the tour cannot get out of step. Left and right arrows still jump chapters.
The Lyrics chapter only annotates what is actually different: the translation, the song credit, Spotify playback, the example dots, and the lyric line count. The tutorial is 17 steps instead of 26.
Fixed the step counter, which was counting the wrong face and showing the wrong number on every question side.

entries.summary: Clarify sense grouping and commonness on cards
detail: Grouped matching two-sense entries, including no/not negation, when they share a context.
Showed compact commonness bars on every collapsed sense group in label mode and used one high-contrast bar colour.
Kept long surface and lemma pairs on one line by fitting their measured widths.

entries.summary: Clarify language and music choices and group skipped-word decks by level
detail: Made language, mode, and music-source choices a clearer sequence with consistent descriptions and Back navigation.
Grouped skipped Fast Track word decks beneath their original levels, in sets of up to 20, with existing card progress on each set.
Kept merged word forms as a note on their shared cards and clarified the empty skipped-deck state.

entries.summary: Make home controls easier to use and clarify review and source icons
detail: Enlarged the top bar, language control, main actions, and set targets; sets now show five per row.
Moved review cards into their own section above skipped Fast Track words and removed the level-suggestion skip control.
Grouped level and set information, simplified Fast Track to its toggle and Details action, and replaced fuzzy source favicons with larger vector marks.

entries.summary: Rename the tile to Rarer uses and link matching dictionary senses
detail: The tile and page now say Rarer uses: senses that show up less often in speech.
Dictionary senses that share an exact gloss or context are grouped, with a small pager when they are otherwise the same shade.

entries.summary: Tighten Other uses, the set scrubber, and skipped Fast Track decks
detail: Rare/other uses now group matching glosses under part-of-speech headings, scroll inside the card, and use the page subtitle to explain they are less common than Uncommon.
The active-set scrubber and settings icon no longer sit in boxes; return-to text still appears on child cards.
Fast Track on the setup page is skipped-word decks of 20, started from small numbered pills.

entries.summary: Show the actual lemma beside each merged word form
detail: Merged form lists show the lemma and its matching translation on the left, with the skipped form and its translation on the right.
The surviving card surface is no longer mistaken for the lemma when it is another inflection.

entries.summary: Fix Rare Sense button opening the card
detail: Moved the part-of-speech label formatter into shared scope so rare dictionary senses render without an error.
Updated app asset versions and the service worker cache to deliver the fix to existing installations.

entries.summary: Deploy Spanish (6k), Portuguese (6k), and Czech (4k) V14 speech decks
detail: Updated speech decks to signed-off v14 with MWE routing.
Deterministic invariant MWE bypass (no 2-way competition) for fixed grammatical locutions.
Ambiguous MWE competition with active_selection_projection: mwe_augmented and dual-written word leaf.
Exact-text embedding caches expanded and verified for Spanish, Portuguese, and Czech.

entries.summary: Align the back lemma chip to the letterforms, not the font em-box
detail: The lemma chip now centres on the surface's cap-height band so it no longer sits low against the word.

entries.summary: Centre the back lemma chip on the headword, colour it by POS, and fold pronominal se into the chip
detail: Back lemma chip is vertically centred with the surface form and uses the active part-of-speech colour.
Pronominal cards no longer drop 'verb with se' onto a second line; se sits inside the lemma chip on the same row.

entries.summary: Keep the coloured POS pill as the icon, drop italics, and put a small quiet lemma chip beside the back headword
detail: Front capsule again uses the real POS pill on the left, with the lemma as a roman label on the right.
Back title is the large surface plus a compact lemma chip — no filled green capsule and no extra vertical bulk.
Lemma text is no longer italic on either face.

entries.summary: Keep the coloured POS pill as the icon, drop italics, and put a small quiet lemma chip beside the back headword
detail: Front capsule again uses the real POS pill on the left, with the lemma as a roman label on the right.
Back title is the large surface plus a compact lemma chip — no filled green capsule and no extra vertical bulk.
Lemma text is no longer italic on either face.

entries.summary: POS-then-lemma nested pill on the card front, and the same compound object on the back with surface then lemma
detail: Front grammar capsule now reads part of speech first, with the lemma in the inner chip on the right, because POS governs the lemma.
Back headword no longer appends the lemma in brackets; an inflected surface and its dictionary form share one nested pill, surface on the left and lemma on the right.
Cards whose surface already is the lemma keep a plain headword, so infinitives and identical forms are not wrapped in an empty compound chip.

entries.summary: Developer deploy audit card with agent & timestamp, Bad Bunny & Rosalía level resolution, and rare senses button fix
detail: Added top-level deploy audit hero card to the Developer tab showing exact change timestamp, authoring LLM agent, human summary in normal text font, and live Service Worker cache status.
Fixed Bad Bunny and Rosalía zero levels bug in lyrics artist mode by removing shadowing module-level activeArtist variable.
Fixed rare senses toggle button clickability by eliminating illegal nested button in section header.
Added strict instructions to CLAUDE.md and WORKING_WITH_JOSH.md requiring all agents to record exact datetime, agent name, and human summary in dev_changelog.json before deploying.

entries.summary: Sense row audit: fixed blank subsense dashes and improved context visibility across CS, PT, and ES
detail: Subsense cells now show metadata pills (grammar, construction, functional relation) even when the row is unselected, instead of a blank em dash.
Preserved real Wiktionary context (e.g. 'myself', 'himself', 'being a part of') that was previously blanket-wiped when the provider context matched the cleaned context.
Functional metadata (purpose, material, origin, direction) now scores high enough to serve as a sense differentiator.
Fixed grouped text sizing: density calculation evaluates worst-case single row instead of summing all rows, upgrading ~1,100 groups to larger font classes.
Blank dashes dropped from 100% to <2% in CS and PT, and to 0% in ES.

entries.summary: Unified Rare Senses & Expressions child card and retired raw example sentence shards
detail: Combined rare dictionary senses and attached multi-word expressions/locutions into a single unified child card with dedicated badges (PHRASE and amber RARE), POS tags, translations, contexts, and canonical examples.
Added on-demand trigger button ('Explore rare senses & expressions →') at the bottom of the card back, with preserved flip navigation on return.
Replaced the obsolete 'More sentences' toggle with 'Rare senses & expressions' in study preferences after a correct card.
Retired un-disambiguated backup sentence shards in favour of verified WSD-assigned occurrences.

entries.summary: Redo set filtering, SRS spacing penalty, smoother card flips/swipes, 7s auto-continue, and larger provenance icons
detail: Updated Redo Set to only redo cards that were missed or skipped in the set, plus any cards that became due for spaced review if time elapsed.
Added SRS premature recall protection: correct answers within 4 hours of a prior exposure do not advance SRS past stage 1, preventing working-memory recall from inflating multi-day review intervals.
Increased deck completion auto-continue hold delay from 5s to 7s.
Modernized card 3D flip easing and swipe gesture thresholds to prevent glitchy transitions and accidental swipes.
Increased dictionary provenance and source icons to 28px for clearer readability.

entries.summary: Deploy ES V12 deck (es-speech-v12-6000x10)
detail: 6,000 cards with 10 display examples using WSD v12-1 with difficulty stratification and tail gating.

entries.summary: Fixed Daily Review loading screen lockup and redesigned Fast Track modal
detail: Fixed full-screen loading screen remaining visible after deck initialization by adding guaranteed dismiss handlers to startDailyReview, next-daily-review, and loadVocabularyData.
Redesigned Fast Track modal with a space-efficient flex layout, bounded height, sticky header/search, and internal smooth scrolling so it never overflows or clips off-screen.

entries.summary: Deploy CS V12 deck (cs-speech-v12-4000x10)
detail: 4,000 cards with 10 display examples using WSD v12-1 with difficulty stratification and tail gating.

entries.summary: Deploy ES V12 deck (es-speech-v12-6000x10)
detail: 6,000 cards with 10 display examples using WSD v12-1 with difficulty stratification and tail gating.

entries.summary: Deploy PT V12 deck (pt-speech-v12-6000x10)
detail: 6,000 cards with 10 display examples using WSD v12-1 with difficulty stratification and tail gating.

entries.summary: Deploy PT V12 deck (pt-speech-v12-6000x10)
detail: 6,000 cards with 10 display examples using WSD v12-1 with difficulty stratification and tail gating.

entries.summary: Deploy PT V12 deck (pt-speech-v12-6000x10)
detail: 6,000 cards with 10 display examples using WSD v12-1 with difficulty stratification and tail gating.

entries.summary: Deploy PT V12 deck (pt-speech-v12-6000x10)
detail: 6,000 cards with 10 display examples using WSD v12-1 with difficulty stratification and tail gating.

entries.summary: Urgency-scored review queue, 100-card daily batches, and sectioned Review Hub
detail: Continuous needfulness score and urgency tiers (Never Mastered, Critical Lapses, Routine Due) derived directly from the SRS schedule and personal error history.
Review queue prioritizes never-mastered cards and severe lapses first, breaking ties by high-frequency word rank so core vocabulary is refreshed ahead of rare words.
Redesigned the setup Review Hub with one-tap tier slices and 100-card daily batches, with a seamless 'Review Next 100' continuation flow on completion.
Optimized review deck loading with an instant fast path, slashing launch time from ~10s to instantaneous (< 30ms) by avoiding full dictionary scans.

entries.summary: Fast Track setup bar streamlined to compact single-row card and modal opening fixed
detail: Fixed Fast Track words modal not opening when clicking 'Browse words' by removing the overriding inline style on #extrasModal.
Eliminated double nested card borders and duplicate header text from the setup screen, reducing the Fast Track bar to a sleek, compact single-row summary.
Added one-tap card clickability and a direct Fast Track settings shortcut when no words are skipped.

entries.summary: Cognate form scoring upgraded with Jaro-Winkler prefix-weighted similarity
detail: Upgraded form similarity scoring to take the best of normalized Levenshtein and Jaro-Winkler, resolving the suffix penalty that kept transparent citation forms (e.g. Spanish 'abandonar', 'comunicar') below threshold while inflections passed.
Cleaned redundant vowel diacritics from Spanish and Portuguese cognate skeleton configs, relying on Unicode NFD strip_accents.
Rebuilt and deployed Spanish-English cognates mapping (31,828 scored surfaces) to workspace and app.

entries.summary: Adaptive spaced repetition, sticky sense-level exceptions, and global daily review
detail: Intervals adapt to learner failure history with soft drops on mistake (down 2 stages instead of resetting to day 0) and graduation to 365 days.

Sense-level knowledge marking in the card modal now treats unmarked senses as known when marking an exception, makes explicit 'No' sticky against whole-card swipes, and adds a Save & Next Card action.
A level-agnostic Daily Review banner on setup provides 1-tap review for all due cards in the language, and dead CEFR fallback paths are removed.

entries.summary: Speech and Lyrics now share saved progress, with an honest Spotify indicator
detail: Equivalent Speech and Lyrics cards now share historical progress by language and displayed word, while preserving existing saved records.
New answers use the latest review state and continue syncing through the deployed progress service across desktop and mobile.
Spotify shows a circular music visualizer only after playback is confirmed; a button press or pending mobile handoff no longer looks like audio is already playing.

entries.summary: Mobile Spotify playback no longer depends on an already-playing phone app
detail: Mobile Lyrics cards now create a Spotify Web Playback device in the browser instead of requiring Spotify Connect to find an active phone session.
The Spotify button activates browser audio directly from the learner's tap, including the user-gesture bridge required by iOS autoplay rules.
Spotify Connect remains available as a fallback when the browser player cannot become ready; Spotify Premium is still required.

entries.summary: Light mode keeps primary study actions readable
detail: The Learn new cards action keeps its filled accent background instead of becoming white with white text.
The correction applies to the shared responsive control, so the action remains legible on desktop and mobile.
Unstarted set choices retain their intended pale light-mode treatment.

entries.summary: Cross-device progress now loads in the deployed app
detail: The live static configuration now includes the public Google Sheets sync endpoint instead of relying on an excluded backend file.
A phone or other new browser can load the same named learner's historical card, knowledge-item, estimate and completed-level progress.
Static deployment validation now rejects builds that omit either progress sync or Spotify's public OAuth client configuration.

entries.summary: Spotify buttons now open sign-in reliably in deployed Lyrics decks
detail: The public Spotify OAuth client ID now ships with static deployments while private backend configuration remains excluded.
Desktop sign-in opens before asynchronous PKCE work can trigger popup blocking, with a full-page fallback; mobile keeps its full-page return-to-card flow.
The Web Playback SDK now loads only after its readiness callback exists, removing a startup race, and missing configuration produces a visible message instead of a silent no-op.

entries.summary: Example credits now favour readable titles over source codes
detail: Resolved film and television names remain clickable without appending their raw IMDb identifier.
Subtitle line numbers remain in raw Card Data for auditing but no longer clutter learner-facing source credits.
An IMDb identifier is shown only when no human title can be resolved.

entries.summary: Speech examples once again identify their film or television source
detail: Fresh release metadata is normalized into the app's provenance view, restoring IMDb links and subtitle line numbers.
A pinned IMDb title layer adds human movie names and resolves television episodes to their parent series.
The active 2,000-card Spanish release has IMDb links for all 5,997 examples and human titles for 5,967 of them.

entries.summary: POS pills now preserve complete grammatical labels
detail: The fixed front-and-back grammar bay is wide enough for two full labels per row, including Adjective and other longer names.
POS text no longer wraps inside a pill.

entries.summary: The POS grid now occupies the same header position on both card faces
detail: The front-face grammar bay has moved from beside the central surface prompt to the fixed top-right header area used on the back.
Its bounded one-row or two-row layout is unchanged.

entries.summary: Part-of-speech labels now use a stable one- or two-row card layout
detail: One or two labels remain together on one centred row, while three or four labels use a compact two-row grid.
The same bounded grammar area is used on both card faces and remains vertically aligned with the headword.
Every label stays readable, the active part of speech remains highlighted, and changing senses does not reorder the labels.

entries.summary: Assigned cards now show only learner-supported senses and honest percentages
detail: Unused dictionary alternatives remain available as audit-only menu evidence instead of appearing as a giant unassigned learner row.
Assigned sense percentages once again total 100%; the hidden remainder bucket can no longer halve them to 50%.
The explicit unassigned fallback remains available for cards that genuinely have no assigned sense.

entries.summary: Multi-headword card backs no longer repeat lemma labels
detail: Each lemma remains visible in its existing part-of-speech and headword row.
Redundant horizontal lemma strips above the corresponding sense rows were removed.
Sense grouping, selection highlighting and source order are unchanged.

entries.summary: The active workspace now has two explicit demonstration decks
detail: French Speech keeps its fresh 200-card Tatoeba release, while Spanish Lyrics keeps a self-contained Bad Bunny-only release.
Spanish Speech and French Lyrics now say they are awaiting a fresh run instead of attempting to load archived evidence.
All other migration runs, source copies, previews and candidates were moved into a dated recoverable archive outside the live workspace.

entries.summary: Artist acceptance now covers French Lyrics, offline decks and playlist restoration
detail: French Lyrics is available from the language-first chooser and opens its real Artist source without loading Speech first.
An explicitly downloaded immutable Lyrics release can launch offline while the active catalogue remains network-authoritative whenever a connection exists.
A fresh named login now restores its saved cross-artist playlist from SongSets, including contributing-artist provenance.

entries.summary: Language choice now leads directly to a lightweight Speech or Lyrics decision
detail: Choosing Spanish no longer loads the Speech release before a learner can select Lyrics; the exact source starts loading only after it is chosen.
Merge Lemmas remains available as learner-facing form grouping, while optional Lyrics, cognate and morphology controls follow explicit language or release capabilities.
Card backs omit a redundant single inert POS label, cognate settings use clearer Include/Exclude wording, and secondary setup guidance is quieter and provenance-accurate.

entries.summary: Preserved Artist assignments are now clearly identified while auditing
detail: Card Data names the exact immutable Lyrics release supplying the active deck.
Historical prompt IDs that are not part of the new registry are labelled retained assignments instead of unregistered models.
Existing example-level method, translation, song and raw-record evidence remains available while clean WSD regeneration stays optional.

entries.summary: Artist data now stays bound to one immutable release
detail: The active Lyrics catalog rewrites vocabulary, examples, songs, artwork and Spotify data to release-versioned URLs before they are loaded.
Offline caches can retain immutable release assets without accidentally serving data from an older active release.
Preview and active releases now use the same loading path; release activation remains an explicit separate action.

entries.summary: Repeated audit flags now remain separate, traceable events
detail: Every flag gesture has an immutable FlagId, so retries deduplicate safely without overwriting a later report on the same card.
Flags include the client build and exact example/source-record identifiers when available.
The shared backend adds open-to-fixed resolution fields while retaining all historical evidence.

entries.summary: Flags now identify their exact release and JSTA is a dedicated audit account
detail: French flags include the immutable release, run, content and layer provenance available at the time of review.
JSTA receives the same information and flagging controls as JST while keeping separate progress.
Choose your own remembers contributing artists as well as exact song IDs through the shared SongSets backend contract.

entries.summary: The existing Fluency app surface now runs against the clean release architecture
detail: The interface and active-set experience are transplanted from the existing app.
French data is mounted from one explicitly active immutable release.
No historical French sentences or WSD assignments are bundled in the code repository.
